Thanks for the note, Lorenzo — understood, and no problem. Below is a recovery plan and concrete options so we can get the hands-on work completed with minimal friction.

Recovery plan (short):
1) Async baseline package (30–45m): we record a 12-minute walkthrough of the POC flow, drop the runbook and routing-checklist, and provide ephemeral creds (scoped to the instance). This will let your team validate config and run primitive prompts without needing everyone live.
2) Hands-on load test (60–90m): schedule when your payments engineer can join. We'll re-run routing checks, step through KV cache and prompt templates, then do a controlled surge to ~200 concurrent sessions.

Proposed concrete slots (PT):
- Option A: Today 2027-05-11 14:00–15:30 (we can still mobilize)
- Option B: Wed 2027-05-12 15:00–16:30 (preferred if you need more prep time)
- Option C: Thu 2027-05-13 09:00–10:30 (early slot if it helps your schedule)

Pre-checks we'll cover before the hands-on: ephemeral creds rotation, CIDR allowlist verification, kernel/quantization fallback plan (if GPU memory spikes), and prompt routing policies. Please confirm which option you prefer and who will be the primary engineer participant (name + calendar email).

Attachments: POC-agenda.pdf, routing-checklist.md, ephemeral-creds.txt (temporary tokens will be rotated after use). We'll also post the async recording to the Drive link below once it's ready.

If you confirm Option B (Wed 5/12 15:00 PT), Dylan and I will reserve the load-test capacity and Marissa will update the post-POC follow-up.

Looking forward to getting this back on track.
— Evelyn
